definition.def: A proportion of a group or an amount is a part of it. [formal]
examples: A large proportion of the dolphins in that area will eventually die. [+ of]
A proportion of the rent is met by the city council. [+ of]

definition.def: The proportion of one kind of person or thing in a group is the number of people or things of that kind compared to the total number of people or things in the group.
examples: The proportion of women in the profession had risen to 17.3%. [+ of]
The radio station has to include a substantial proportion of classical music.

definition.def: The proportion of one amount to another is the relationship between the two amounts in terms of how much there is of each thing.
examples: Women's bodies tend to have a higher proportion of fat to water. [+ to]

definition.def: If you refer to the proportions of something, you are referring to its size, usually when this is extremely large. [written]
examples: In the tropics plants grow to huge proportions.

definition.def: If you refer to the proportions in a work of art or design, you are referring to the relative sizes of its different parts.
examples: You can vary the relative proportions of things in a picture very simply.

definition.def: If something is small or large in proportion to something else, it is small or large when compared with that thing.
examples: Children have relatively larger heads than adults in proportion to the rest of their body.

definition.def: If one thing increases or decreases in proportion to another thing, it increases or decreases to the same degree as that thing.
examples: The pressure in the cylinders would go up in proportion to the boiler pressure.

definition.def: If you say that something is out of all proportion to something else, you think that it is far greater or more serious than it should be.
examples: The punishment was out of all proportion to the crime.

definition.def: If you get something out of proportion, you think it is more important or worrying than it really is. If you keep something in proportion, you have a realistic view of how important it is.
examples: Everything just got blown out of proportion.
We've got to keep this in proportion.

definition.def: If someone has a sense of proportion, they know what is really important and what is not.
examples: We must not lose our sense of proportion.
